title: Christian Braun Says How Nuggets Can Help Their Defense After Early Struggles

Christian Braun Says How Nuggets Can Help Their Defense After Early Struggles

 Arion Armeniakos Partner Nov 21, 2026 12:12 AM Published Nov 21, 2026 12:12 AM The Nuggets showed themselves what they're capable of when they lock in defensively against the Celtics. 
 More Videos The Denver Nuggets recorded one of their biggest wins of the season so far on Wednesday, defeating the Boston Celtics 105-101 at Ball Arena. 
 It was their third win in the last four games, improving their record to 8-5. 
 But most importantly, fueled by a halftime reset, the Nuggets proved to themselves just how effective their defense can be. 
 Locked In
 Christopher Hanewinckel-Imagn Images The Nuggets trailed the Celtics 61-49 at the break, with Jayson Tatum erupting for 20 points. 
 Related stories
 After the interval, Denver held Tatum to just four points on 2-for-6 shooting the rest of the way, erasing Boston's advantage with a 31-19 third-quarter run. 
 As a team, the Nuggets limited the Celtics to just a 25 percent success rate from beyond the arc (11-for-44). 
 "I think whenever we are up and touching people, that's when we're at our best," Christian Braun said of his team's defensive improvement. "In the second half, we went to another level with that. Changing our levels with [Nikola] Jokic, mixing things up, showing different coverages, trying to show guys different things. 
 "Getting physical and attacking the ball helps start our offense, and I think we are okay in transition, but we have to be ready." 
 And there lies the key to the Nuggets' success. Collective defense and role players stepping up. When they get both, they can compete with anybody. When they don't, they struggle to find consistency. 
 Red Hot Second Half
 Christopher Hanewinckel-Imagn Images The Nuggets came out of halftime as a different team. 
 They tied the game at 80-80 going into the fourth quarter with a scorching hot third quarter on both ends of the floor, despite only shooting 7-for-31 from deep on the night. 
 Jokic poured in 12 of his 24 points in the third as Denver went on a 20-4 run at one juncture in the frame. Jamal Murray added three of his four steals in the period. The Nuggets also forced Tatum into five turnovers in the second half. 
 Denver's colder blood prevailed down the stretch. The Nuggets finally got what they were signing up for from veteran DeMar DeRozan , whose 13 fourth-quarter points — including 10 straight — helped the hosts outscore the Celtics by four. 
 Christopher Hanewinckel-Imagn Images DeRozan led the bench with 18 points in 25 minutes, shooting 5-for-11 from the field and 7-for-8 from the line. It was his second-highest-scoring game of the season. 
 Jokic added eight rebounds and nine assists to his tally. Murray posted 21 points and seven rebounds. 
 Braun and Aaron Gordon set the tone for Denver's supporting cast. Braun poured in 15 points, while Gordon added 13 points and eight rebounds. 
 Circling back to Braun's comments on the Nuggets' defense, they simply need to be better more often because of their lack of offensive star power. 
 They're currently 13th in the NBA in points allowed (112.2), 12th in opposing field goal percentage (45.8), and 17th in three-point percentage (35.5), while giving up 13.7 offensive rebounds per game (27th). 
 If the Nuggets are to have a chance in the West, ranking in the middle of the pack in most major defensive categories might not be enough.
